WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND BOOKKEEPING: a block that is finished and merged but authored `open` is offered again by /next, counted as outstanding by every board, and gates any block depending on it. Every path built on it points somewhere that does not exist. FOUND 2026-08-25 by hand-verifying each entry the sweep reported CLEARED before deleting it, rather than trusting the verdict. FIVE entries in this one file were affected, in BOTH directions: (a) FALSE CLEAR, the dangerous direction -- `disjoint-files-rule-needs-a-true-justification` and `authored-checks-use-rg-which-is-not-on-the-engines-path` both wrap the path in `! grep ...`, so a grep against a nonexistent path fails, the negation inverts it to exit 0, and the entry reports CLEARED while the finding is live. `disjoint-files` would have been deleted on this sweep: its '**Under review:**' marker is still at docs/workflows/index.md:174 and the three-way decision it names is still open. carryover.text: `scripts/escalation.schema.json`'s `verified_at_sha` is documented only as "The short git SHA at write time" and never names WHICH repo's SHA. HQ's `scripts/roadmap_sweep.py:248` computes the comparison SHA as `git_head_sha(root)` where `root` is the BRAIN root, so a cross-repo escalation -- whose `verified_by` command cds into a sub-repo and correctly stamps that sub-repo's HEAD -- can NEVER match and is permanently flagged `stale: true` ("verified_at_sha is behind current HEAD; re-verify before acting"). CONSEQUENCE: every cross-repo escalation is mislabelled stale, which trains readers to ignore the stale flag -- the same erosion that retired the Stop/Notification hook. RAISED by agentic-portfolio-3f (commander lane) 2026-08-28 as a FINDING against this lane's own BT.2.A escalation, and INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED HERE before filing rather than taken on the sender's word, per the ping-agent verify-before-acting rule: `scripts/escalation.schema.json:74-77` carries the repo-less description; `scripts/roadmap_sweep.py:248` reads `sha = git_head_sha(root, runner=git_runner)`; and the two SHAs are structurally incapable of matching (brain `d9374158` vs `core/mev` `2032077`, measured the same minute). THE ROOT IS AMBIGUITY, NOT A BUG ON ONE SIDE: the schema (base-template's) and the sweep (HQ's) disagree, and neither is self-evidently wrong -- so the fix is to DECIDE which repo the field names, state it in the schema description, and make the sweep read it that way. Fixing only the sweep leaves the next author guessing again. Owner is base-template because the schema is base-template's; the sweep change is HQ's half and must be filed there once the call is made.

Result: E_GRAPH_DANGLING_RELATED red-gated the ENTIRE corpus, so every other lane's push gate failed on a bastion file until it was fixed (47f5cdd9, ~15 minutes). /begin-orchestration's rule 1 already forbids exactly this ('a related: target must resolve to a real doc_id on a document that has actually been crawled, never a carryover slug or an invented id'), but that rule lives in the orchestration command, which the SDLC engines never read — the engine only ever sees the task text. The fix belongs upstream in base-template (either /generate-tasks emitting the constraint into any task that authors a .md, or the engines reading it), not in this repo; filed here because this lane is where it bit. CORROBORATION, same day: this is not a /generate-tasks bug, it is a corpus-wide authoring gap, and the narrow framing above understates it. THREE cross-repo `related:` red-gates on 2026-08-24, across two lanes and both authoring modes. (1) bastion BA.21.C task 5, agent-authored, invented `ba-21-c` from a block id. (2) bastiel `brain:us-gtm-icp-brief` on a bastiel planning doc, hand-authored. The generalizable rule all three violate is one sentence -- a bare doc_id resolves only within the AUTHORING repo, so any cross-repo target must be qualified `<repo>:<doc_id>` -- and it is currently stated only in docs/okf-frontmatter.md and /begin-orchestration's rule 1, neither of which is in front of someone writing a decision file or a task spec. carryover.text: cargo audit (a gating harness.json check) fails on RUSTSEC-2026-0258 (published 2026-08-17): h2 0.3.27 accepts unbounded empty DATA frames, low severity, denial-of-service class (unbounded memory growth or a panic if a peer sends empty DATA frames without draining). Pulled in transitively: actix-http -> actix-web -> engine-serve. Patched only in h2 >= 0.4.16; confirmed via `cargo update -p actix-web/-p actix-http --dry-run` that the latest actix-http compatible with our Cargo.toml (3.13.3) still resolves h2 0.3.27 — actix-web's whole 3.x/4.x HTTP stack never migrated off h2 0.3 (pre-hyper-1.0), so there is no cargo update or Cargo.toml version-bump fix available today. The real fix is an actix-web major upgrade (or a framework swap), a separate breaking-change piece of work across every engine-serve handler, discovered 2026-08-19 while closing out EN.ticket.otel-pane-telemetry. Real-world exposure depends on whether engine-serve's actual HttpServer::bind() (which lives in the consuming binary, not in this repo — grep for HttpServer::new/.bind() across crates/ here turns up nothing) is Tailscale-only, per HQ.ticket.tailscale-bind-and-token-rotation's stated rule ("do not ship a terminal node onto a listener bound 0.0.0.0 behind a dev token") — not independently reverified from this repo.  UPDATE 2026-08-21 (autonomous-foundation lane): the 'unfixable' half is now DISPROVED, and the gating half is resolved. (a) engine-rs's cargo-audit check was set gates:false — its command ends in `|| true` and therefore cannot return non-zero, so gating on it was a contradiction that had already bailed a block on its OUTPUT (see sdlc-task-triage-bails-on-non-gating-check-output). Advisories are still reported every run. (b) A real fix EXISTS without any actix major upgrade: `http2` is an actix-web DEFAULT feature, so declaring actix-web with default-features=false plus the other seven defaults drops h2 out of the graph entirely (20 lines out of Cargo.lock; `cargo tree -i h2` -> 'did not match any packages'). Verified on branch scratch/h2-experiment (e77b6a4): cargo audit exits 0 and fmt/clippy/build/nextest all pass (2537 tests, 17 skipped). Safe because bastion serve calls `.bind(&addr)` with no bind_rustls/bind_openssl anywhere in the workspace, so HTTP/2 can only ever be h2c prior-knowledge (browsers do not do this), and reqwest is already declared without the http2 feature. Residual risk: a future TLS terminator requiring h2 to origin — none exists. NOT engine-rs-only: core/bastion reports the same h2 0.3.27 PLUS h2 0.4.15 (also below the 0.4.16 fix line) and crossbeam-epoch 0.9.18, so adopting this needs a fleet decision, not a one-repo edit. The branch is unmerged and awaiting that decision.

carryover.text: `fleet_concurrency_check.py`'s idempotent-refresh heartbeat is UNREACHABLE in normal use, so any lane running longer than the 90-minute TTL silently loses its slot and the fleet cap stops enforcing anything — while `register` keeps returning `allowed: true`, which reads as a clean green. Verified at source 2026-08-21, not taken on report. `_lock_path` (line 185) is `{repo}__{pid}.json` — keyed on repo AND pid. `pid` defaults to `os.getpid()`, the SHORT-LIVED writer process, which the script's own comment concedes 'is gone by the time any other process checks it'. So every invocation writes a NEW file under a NEW pid, `already_registered` (line 265, matching on `_path`) is essentially never true, and the heartbeat branch at line 289 — whose stated job is 'it bumps started_at so a long lane's slot doesn't age past the TTL out from under it' — never runs unless the caller passes an explicit `--pid`. `/begin-orchestration`'s documented invocation does not. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: `.fleet-locks/` was EMPTY at 20:54 with two live engine-rs lanes plus bastion and okf-core lanes registered hours earlier; every entry had aged out at 90 minutes (`_sweep_stale` line 189: a `pid_source: "self"` entry ignores pid liveness by design and expires on TTL alone). Both engine-rs sessions believed they still held slots. CORRECTS A PEER REPORT that framed this as 'register is idempotent-refresh, so a second session for the same repo silently bumps the same entry and two lanes show as one' — that is backwards: different pid means a different path, so a second session consumes a SECOND slot, not the same one. The real failure is the opposite (slots vanish, cap under-counts), and a fix built on the reported framing would have made it worse. FIX SHAPE: give the heartbeat a stable key that survives across invocations (repo+category, or a session-supplied id) rather than the writer's pid, or have `/begin-orchestration` pass a real long-lived `--pid`. Owner is base-template; the script lives there and every repo consumes it. INTERIM WORKAROUND, in use by the engine-rs lane from 2026-08-21 until this is fixed: re-run `register --repo <name>` PERIODICALLY for as long as the lane runs. Each call writes a fresh entry under a new pid, which is what keeps a slot present past the 90-minute TTL — the documented heartbeat cannot fire, so manual re-registration is the only thing standing in for it. Note the cost of the workaround: it leaves stale sibling entries until they age out, so the store can briefly OVER-count the same repo. Over-counting fails safe (a lane waits); the unfixed behaviour fails open (the cap enforces nothing). A successor lane in this repo must re-register at briefing rather than assuming an earlier session's slot survives.

carryover.text: The four `held_session::real_tmux_*` integration tests fail on CI and pass locally FOR THE WRONG REASON, and the local green is an artifact of leaked state rather than working code. THREE FACTS, each verified 2026-08-22, none taken on report. (1) MECHANISM: `ensure_tmux_server` (tests/it/held_session.rs:112) creates a throwaway session and IMMEDIATELY kills it (`new_session(&boot)` then `kill_session(&boot)`, both with `let _ =` so failures are swallowed). Killing the LAST session on a tmux server terminates the server. Demonstrated directly on an isolated socket: `tmux -L probe new-session -d -s boot_a` then `tmux -L probe kill-session -t boot_a` leaves `no server running`. So the helper that exists to ENSURE a server is the thing that destroys it whenever no other session happens to be alive. (2) NO ISOLATION: `crates/term-core/src/tmux.rs` passes no `-L`/`-S` socket flag anywhere, so every `TmuxDriver` in every test process shares the ONE default tmux server, alongside any the developer is using. nextest runs a process per test in parallel, so one test's boot-session cleanup can kill the server out from under another mid-test — which is exactly the CI failure text: `real tmux creates the throwaway session: ExitError { code: 1, stderr: "server exited unexpectedly" }` and `list_sessions failed: no tmux server running`. Consistent with a race rather than a deterministic break: on the failing CI run one of the four passed and three failed. (3) WHY LOCAL IS GREEN, AND WHY THAT IS THE WORST PART: this machine has 492 LEAKED `eng-en10a-held-session-it-*` sessions on the default server, the oldest from 2026-08-18 (`KillOnDrop` does not fire when a test panics or a run is aborted). They keep the server alive permanently, so the boot-session kill never removes the last session and the race never fires. A CLEAN machine — every CI runner, and any fresh clone — behaves like CI. The local suite has therefore been self-masking since at least 2026-08-18. NOT A REGRESSION FROM ANY BLOCK: CI ran these same tests green on 2026-08-20 (run 32405148493, 2521/2521) and red on 2026-08-22 (run 32567159015, 2094 passed / 3 failed) on the IDENTICAL runner image (ubuntu-24.04, Version 20260729.566, checked both runs) — what changed is the suite growing 2521 -> 2806 tests, which reshuffled nextest's scheduling so the four now overlap where they previously did not. LIKELY FIX: give the test driver its own `-L <unique>` socket per run so the suite never touches the default server, and stop killing the boot session (or drop `ensure_tmux_server` entirely in favour of a socket the test owns). Both touch term-core's production `tmux.rs`, so this wants its own block, not a drive-by. SEPARATELY: the 492 leaked sessions should be reaped, and `KillOnDrop` hardened so a panicking test still cleans up. CI is currently RED ON MAIN for this reason; PR #50 was merged with --admin over it on the operator's explicit call, after confirming the failure predates and is unrelated to EN.11.N. *** CONFIRMED AND TICKETED 2026-08-22, after the 492 sessions were reaped: the failure now REPRODUCES LOCALLY and the self-masking loop is proven. Clean default server -> `cargo nextest run -p engine-core --test it held_session::real_tmux` fails 3 of 4 with the exact CI error; rerun immediately without cleaning -> 4 of 4 PASS, because the failing run leaked four sessions that keep the server alive; clean again -> fails again. Three cycles, same result each time. So the tests pass if and only if a session already exists, and every failing run manufactures the condition that makes the NEXT run green — which is why nobody caught it. Note the full suite still reports 2806/2806 even from clean, because other concurrent tmux tests keep the server up; the full-suite green is therefore timing-dependent, not evidence. Fix tracked as EN.ticket.real-tmux-tests-need-an-isolated-socket.

carryover.text: fleet_concurrency_check.py's register() refuses on ANY non-stale `kind: exclusive` lease held by a different agent — its own docstring says "in ANY category and regardless of whether `repo` is heavy-gated at all -- this is fleet-exclusive admission control" (_find_blocking_exclusive_lease, line ~300). But /begin-orchestration Step 4 instructs EVERY lane to take `kind: exclusive` ("exclusive for a lane that will commit — every real lane"), and lease.schema.json scopes exclusivity BY REPO: "two 'exclusive' leases on the same repo are not [legal]", with `repo` documented as the field duplicate-detection groups by. The script promotes to the fleet what the schema and the command both scope to one repo, and the script wins at runtime. CONSEQUENCE, and it is worse than 'too broad': the refusal is UNREACHABLE-BY-DESIGN under the documented procedure — if every real lane takes an exclusive lease and any one non-stale exclusive lease refuses all registers, fleet concurrency is capped at ONE lane whenever leases are fresh, so the per-category caps (2 browser-automation, 4 native-build, D66) can NEVER be exercised. MEASURED 2026-08-23: four lanes ran concurrently that night only because leases kept going STALE. THE STALENESS BUG WAS MASKING THE EXCLUSIVITY BUG — fixing the heartbeat gap alone would make the fleet strictly worse by serialising it. Observed live: three exclusive leases on disk at once (base-template/base-template-f8, brain/agentic-portfolio-64, engine-rs/engine-rs-37). CORRECTED 2026-08-23 — only NON-STALE leases block: _non_stale_exclusive_leases (line 280) drops anything past the 5400s threshold, so base-template-f8's abandoned lease was skipped, not blocking. The fleet is quiesced by whichever lane is currently RUNNING and un-quiesces when it closes; there is nothing to expire and no lease for an operator to delete. Saying 'abandoned leases have parked the fleet' would prompt an unnecessary and destructive manual deletion. engine-rs-37 bumped its own heartbeat to clear a stale-claim complaint and thereby re-armed the block on everyone, i.e. following both documented maintenance instructions is worse than following neither. Reported and independently source-verified by engine-rs-37 (their evidence, cited with permission); filed from HQ because rule 6 stops an HQ lane at base-template's boundary. *** THIRD LAYER, and it is the cheap fix — VERIFIED IN SOURCE 2026-08-23. _find_blocking_exclusive_lease() DOES exempt the lease's own holder, but only when the caller identifies itself: line 305 states that "a requester with no agent identity supplied (`requester_agent is None`) can never match, by design". **/begin-orchestration Step 3's documented invocation omits `--agent`** — line 162 (`register --repo <this-repo-name> --category <category>`) and line 171, which instructs the periodic heartbeat as "repeat the same register --repo ... --category" call. So requester_agent is None on every documented invocation, the holder exemption can never engage, and A LANE FOLLOWING STEPS 3 AND 4 EXACTLY IS REFUSED BY ITS OWN LEASE WHENEVER IT TRIES TO HEARTBEAT. Reproduced live by engine-rs-37: register --repo engine-rs --category native-build returned allowed:false with a reason string naming engine-rs-37 itself as the blocker; adding --agent engine-rs-37 to the identical command in the same second returned allowed:true. THE THREE LAYERS COMPOUND: (1) exclusivity is repo-scoped in lease.schema.json and fleet-scoped in the script; (2) Step 4 tells every lane to take `exclusive`, so every lane trips layer 1; (3) Step 3 omits `--agent`, so the exemption that would have made layer 1 survivable never fires. MITIGATION, CORRECTED 2026-08-23 — THE EARLIER VERSION OF THIS ENTRY OVERCLAIMED IT AND THE OVERCLAIM WAS THE DANGEROUS PART. Adding `--agent <agent_name>` to Step 3's two register invocations in /begin-orchestration (and its .agents mirror) fixes ONLY the self-block-on-heartbeat case: line 310 exempts solely the agent that HOLDS the blocking lease. Measured twice by two lanes — `register --repo bastion --category native-build --agent bastion-61` and `register --repo brain --category native-build --agent agentic-portfolio-64` were BOTH refused, each naming engine-rs-37's lease. So `--agent` does nothing for a cross-lane block, which is the case that actually stops work. THE IMMEDIATE MITIGATION FOR CROSS-LANE BLOCKING IS LAYER (1), scoping the refusal to the requesting repo, and THERE IS NO DOCUMENTATION-ONLY WORKAROUND FOR IT. Shipping the `--agent` edit alone lets someone watch their own heartbeat start working and conclude the defect is handled while every cross-lane block remains — the same retire-by-inference trap this entry's clears_when guards against, arriving from the other direction. Note the agent name must come from the transport-stamped identity Step 4 already requires, never a self-reported one. *** WHICH FIX TO MAKE IS A DELIBERATE CHOICE, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL (raised by bastion-61). The script and its own docstring AGREE with each other — line 333 says "regardless of whether `repo` is heavy-gated at all -- this is fleet-exclusive admission control" — and both disagree with lease.schema.json, which scopes exclusivity per-repo ("no one else may hold any lease ON IT"). So there are two coherent fixes pointing opposite ways, and a reviewer will pick one by accident depending on which file they open first: reading the schema gives "the script is too broad, scope the refusal to the requesting repo"; reading the docstring gives "fleet-exclusive admission is INTENDED, and the real defect is Step 4 telling every lane to write `exclusive`, which makes every ordinary lane a fleet-wide mutex". Whoever fixes this must choose between those two authorities on purpose and say which one they are honouring. *** ALSO RETRACTED, by its own author: bastion-61's order-dependence explanation (Step 3 registering before Step 4's lease, so only re-registrations are refused) is withdrawn — the exemption covers a lane's own lease only, so a sibling's fresh lease still refuses a first register, and their timestamps show both sibling leases postdated their first register. The staleness-masking explanation above is the one the evidence supports.

A lane running under a non-zsh shell (bash, sh, a CI runner, any harness that does not launch the user's zsh login shell) will not see the pair and gets `C006 bot 'lane' is not configured` — indistinguishable, from the agent's side, from the operator never having created the bot. CORRECTED 2026-08-24 after bastion-1d failed to reproduce this entry's original claim, and they were right: this entry first asserted that a Claude Code Bash tool call cannot see the vars because 'that shell is not zsh'. THAT IS FALSE ON THIS MACHINE — the Bash tool runs the user's login shell, which IS zsh (`$0` = /bin/zsh), and `env | grep -c '^BASTION_LANE_'` returns 2 with positive control `grep -c '^HOME='` = 1. The original measurement of 0 was real but was taken at a DIFFERENT MOMENT: the exports were then in `~/.zshrc`, not `~/.zshenv`. That is the finding that actually held — zsh sources `.zshrc` for INTERACTIVE shells only, so a non-interactive lane call saw nothing, which is why the exports were moved to `.zshenv` (sourced by every zsh invocation) and why `.zshrc` must not be used for these. Conflating the two moments produced a wrong attribution that would have sent the next person hitting C006 under zsh chasing the wrong variable. SO THE REMAINING HAZARD IS REAL BUT HYPOTHETICAL HERE, not observed: no lane on this machine currently runs under a non-zsh shell. (2) Mid-block instability: /sdlc-task commits per task, so an upstream repo's main is LEGITIMATELY red between task commits — bastion-ui measured okf-core in the window between task 1 and task 2 of OK.ticket.carryover-kind-typed-enum and got a real E0277 that had ceased to exist minutes later. Compounding both: a break migrates. This one walked okf-core -> mev -> bastion as each repo adapted, so three measurements the same day named three different owners and each was correct when taken. Consequence: a false result from such a predicate is evidence that SOMETHING upstream is red, never evidence about the entry it is attached to. Attach an error-class or path discriminator to any such predicate, measure against the upstream repo's last close-out commit rather than HEAD, and never let a machine flip an entry on the bare exit code.

The command therefore fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the finding, and the entry is reported `unmet` — which reads as 'the defect is still live'. Such an entry can never clear, no matter how thoroughly it is fixed. This is a DIFFERENT mechanism from okf-core:command-exits-zero-predicates-are-unsound-across-a-live-fleet, which covers transitive build scope and mid-block instability — that one makes a predicate answer the wrong question, this one stops it answering at all, and the failure direction is opposite (that one can clear an entry falsely, this one can never clear a real one). Fix either by running the predicate from the brain root, or by rejecting a relative path at author time.
